question:
**Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

You care for him / even more than for myself, / he cried bitterly.
solution:
Here the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The part that contains a grammatical error is: **even more than for myself.**
 
• The correct pronoun usage should be** "even more than for me." **
 
• The pronoun** "myself"** is a** reflexive pronoun**, which is used when the subject and object of a sentence are the same person.
 
• However, in this case, the subject is "**You**" (referring to the person being addressed), and the object is "**him**." Therefore, the correct pronoun to use is the objective pronoun "**me**" instead of "**myself**."
 
• Example of correct pronoun usage:
 
 
• I care for him even more than for myself. (Correct)
 
• They invited me to the party. (Correct)
 
 
 
• Incorrect pronoun usage:
 
 
• I care for himself even more than for myself. (Incorrect)
 
• They invited myself to the party. (Incorrect)
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the correct option would be **3) even more than for myself, **as it contains the grammatical error in the pronoun usage.

 

**The corrected sentence would be**: *"You care for him **even more than for me**__*, *he cried bitterly."*
